The sealing time remains fixed at No. 50, and the key never leaves his waist. Tolerance is flat compared with the prior (0.73), with margin still remaining.

plot_point: Before the distribution point, Lin Zhao had already publicly announced that the main warehouse had a registered total of 112 cans and 201 and a half portions, and on the spot delivered in full the two portions on Aunt Zhao’s tag, crossing out the two lines; the conversion dispute has been closed through “admit the error, retract it, record the account, show the evidence”, and the distribution process is in the execution phase of “numbers already announced, first portion already issued, stickers awaiting placement, accounts awaiting balancing”.

Lin Zhao publicly lays the roster and ledger side by side, publicly fills in the quantities for the four newly registered residents—three full shares and one half share, totaling three and a half shares—and publicly explains the rounding algorithm and where the remainder goes: one hundred twelve cans divided by two hundred one and a half shares gives fifty-five percent; round down to half a can; the remainder decreases from eleven and a quarter cans to nine and a quarter cans; three and a half shares convert to one and three-quarter cans and are allocated as two cans; with a denominator of two hundred five shares, half a can per share gives one hundred two and a half cans, with a remainder of nine and a quarter cans—thus nailing “half a can per share”, the rounding, and the destination of the remainder onto the paper.

Lin Zhao writes the three items Aunt Zhao recited onto paper slips without adding a single word, and adds one line: "If the counts for the three items do not match by evening, the difference will be borne by the handler Lin Zhao, explained publicly, and not apportioned to any ration card number"; he folds the paper and presses it under the first page of the ledger, agreeing that in the evening they will take it out face to face, check the items one by one, and after confirming them, press a handprint and copy another version to post on the pillar; verbally, he explains that the cover of the new east-warehouse account should first record the date, the names of those present, and the four characters "not yet counted," and only after the cover is written will they wrap it with hemp cord and seal the door.

Aunt Zhao linked the four lines on the paper slip into her own verification checklist—“Good, I’ll come by at dusk and check them one by one”, “the seal strips, nine intact cans, two spoonfuls into the pot, the East Warehouse’s new ledger—not one item can be off”, “and don’t you forget Dr. Li’s side either”; Lin Zhao listed “add the missing name to the No. 30 badge roster” as the fifth item, “ask the duty staff to engrave the name onto the No. 30 badge” as the sixth, and “if the duty staff leave no written name, Lin Zhao will go negotiate in person tomorrow morning” as the seventh, then tied the items and the badge together and handed them to Aunt Zhao.

Lin Zhao publicly reissues six clean-water tablets owed to No. 94 from the day before yesterday and crosses out that line. Facing the challenge “There's still quite a lot in the box—didn't you say this morning that there were none today,” she uses “What I said this morning was that they wouldn't be issued with today's shares; I didn't say there were none in the storehouse” to separate “there are some” from “they should be issued today,” and states that where the remaining tablets go requires the committee's approval, and not a single tablet will be deducted from the round the day after tomorrow.

This turn: Aunt Zhao leaves the shed after only saying, “Seal the door at No. 50, don’t just remember handing things out and forget that; I’ll take the slip to the duty shed this afternoon and come back to reconcile the accounts at dusk”; Lin Zhao presses the ball of hemp thread onto line fifty of the roster, making it tangible evidence, publicly admits, “In three years I haven’t handed out a single portion wrong—not because my brain is good, but because all these years I’ve done nothing but this kind of stupid work,” and publicly teaches the three newly registered people to identify the spoon, recognize the signed receipt, and have the child press his own fingerprint, then reports the count: “Four newly registered people, three and a half portions, seven loose spoons.”

Lin Zhao must complete the remaining box openings and actual counts, post today's total distribution number and cutoff tag number on the shed pillar, and advance distribution in order; when issuing to number fifty, she must go publicly to the east warehouse door and wrap hemp cord around it to seal the door (without unlocking it first, and with the key never leaving her waist); before sunset, she must fulfill the east warehouse clear count (ask Doctor Li to be present, pick out bulging rusted cans, and post counts in the two categories of distributable/discarded); and she must close the account line for the extra allotment to Auntie Zhao's son with the voucher before noon.
attention: The most psychologically significant point in this turn is Auntie Zhao’s line before leaving the shed: “No. 50 is to be sealed; don’t just remember to hand things out and forget that.” She nails the time for sealing the door as Lin Zhao’s obligation. Lin Zhao responds by saying, “The ball of thread is pressing on the line for No. 50. I check each line downward one by one; when I check to the point where I bump into this ball of thread, my hand stops,” turning the to-do item from memory into tangible physical evidence. This is the pivot of the small migration in this turn: the plot-level conflict has not changed, but “don’t forget” has been externalized into a physical object.

“I haven’t issued a single share wrong in three years, not because I’m smart, but because all these years I’ve done nothing but these stupid things—pressing thread bundles, drawing horizontal lines, writing to-do items at the top of the page”—Lin Zhao publicly lays out the basis of trust for others to see, responding to the snickering under the shed about “still needing string to remind himself”. This is one self-explanation he voluntarily offers in this turn.

The three newly registered people publicly acknowledged the ladle and the signed receipt: Lin Zhao ladled it in person, scraped it level in person, poured it into the bowl in person, and reported the count: “four newly registered people, three and a half shares, seven loose ladles”; when that child pressed a handprint, his mother stopped him for a moment, and Lin Zhao said, “Let her press it. She has a badge, so she has this one press” — making “here, we don’t recognize qualification, we recognize the account” land on a child’s handprint.

After the box of water purification tablets is seen in public, Lin Zhao separates “there are” from “they should be issued today”, holds the line with “I won’t promise what I can’t promise”, and cannot state the remaining number—if he stated it, it would be equivalent to promising their destination on behalf of the committee. The committee’s confidential purpose for reserving the water purification tablets still has not leaked by a single word, but it has been forced to the edge of the table.

Aunt Zhao will take the strip to the duty shed in the afternoon to have the notches added, and in the evening bring the original strip over to check the accounts item by item; she named both tasks and said neither may be missed. Lin Zhao must keep the seal strip safe, set out the nine full tins and two spoonfuls on the counter, and write the cover of the East Storehouse’s new ledger first, waiting for her to come and compare them one by one.

“If the committee does not allow it to be issued, they still have to write the reason clearly” still presses down under the shed. Lin Zhao has already nailed down the public wording as “transcribe the original words; write down who said them and on what day; if they only throw out the two characters ‘not approved,’ then write: not approved, no reason given, handler Lin Zhao”—one layer closer to that sheet of paper: he knows very well that after the East Storehouse is counted, the portion that can be issued will most likely have to be folded into tomorrow’s share, but before the regulations come down, he cannot endorse tomorrow’s numbers on their behalf.

Latent_signals: trust :: His trust in Auntie Zhao remains the kind of “I lay it out for you to see; you verify it yourself”, and in this turn it becomes more solid: she leaves after only saying “don't forget”, which is equivalent to handing the verification checklist back into his hands. He no longer needs to persuade her; he only needs to press the ball of thread onto the line for No. 50 and nail down the gate-sealing time. The same is true for the queue—he publicly accepts, “I haven't issued a single share wrong in three years; not because my head is good, but because all these years I've done nothing but this kind of stupid work”, laying out the basis of trust for others to see.; vigilance :: His attention is still spread across the whole queue and the three pending tasks: while answering Auntie Zhao's “don't forget”, he must also set the gate-sealing at No. 50, point out the supplemental-notching line to the people on duty, and make sure the seven items match one by one by evening. This turn adds one more place: the three newly registered people must be taught on the spot to recognize the ladle and the signed claim slips, and when that child presses his handprint, he must stop the mother's hesitation.; contradiction_risk :: In this turn, “there's still quite a bit in the box—didn't you say this morning there was none today?” pushes the gap between “there is” and “should be issued today” onto the surface. He must align the words by saying, “What I said this morning was that it wouldn't be issued along with the shares today; I didn't say there was none in the storeroom”, otherwise it would constitute a public inconsistency. The posted numbers, the number tags that have been issued up to, the actual count from opening the box, the reason for “not allowed”, the fixed amount for the new names, the carryover of the remainder, the physical correspondence between whole tins and opened cans ladled out by spoonfuls, and the wording of the two paper slips—these eight things still must fit together without the slightest gap.; user.trust :: She trusts that this person will leave the gate-sealing until No. 50 and keep the original slips for her to check item by item, but this trust still carries the force of “I have to keep watch over it myself”. Now even “gate-sealing at No. 50” has been made by him into something visible, with the ball of thread pressing it down on the register; there is one more piece of evidence held in her sight. But the lock is still there, and the key has not been given to her.; user.vigilance :: What she is watching is still the verifiable paper records and physical objects: gate-sealing at No. 50, supplemental notching at the duty shed in the afternoon, and checking the accounts item by item against the original slips in the evening; all three have been named and are not allowed to be missed. Now the gate-sealing time is pressed down on the register by the ball of thread, and the new residents have also been taught in public to recognize the ladle—nothing she is watching has decreased; each item has simply gained one more piece of verifiable evidence.; user.anxiety :: Today's two shares are in the bag, the names have also been read aloud in public, and the handprints have been pressed; this part has landed. But that string is still taut—the afternoon supplemental notching and the evening inspection of the seal strips, neither is allowed to be missed. Now the gate-sealing time has been pressed down by the ball of thread, and the new residents have also been taught in public to recognize the ladle, so it has loosened by half an inch; the opening called “tomorrow” is still there.

goal_tracking.trigger_summary: Lin Zhao completed the physical count, publicly reported the total, delivered the two portions on Auntie Zhao’s tags in full, admitted the mistake and withdrew the clerical slip, disclosed the uncertainty about the east warehouse and gave a commitment to count it clearly, then fixed the three items Auntie Zhao recited into paper labels and added a self-assumption clause, set the door-sealing time at No. 50, and pressed the ball of thread onto the roster; in this turn, Auntie Zhao turned the four lines on the paper label into her own verification checklist and nailed “sealing the door at No. 50” as Lin Zhao’s obligation. Lin Zhao must keep the sealing strip ready, set out the nine full cans and two scoops on the counter, write the cover of the new east-warehouse ledger first, complete the remaining box-opening physical counts, post today’s total distributed and the cutoff tag number on the shed post, distribute up to No. 50 and publicly seal the door, fulfill the clear east-warehouse count before sunset, and close the ledger line for the extra issue to Auntie Zhao’s son with a receipt before noon. The goal has not changed; it has merely advanced from “make good on the reported numbers, explain the conversion thoroughly, count the east warehouse clearly, and balance the accounts” to “keep the sealing strip ready, set out the nine full cans and two scoops at the physical-object level, write the cover of the new east-warehouse ledger first, nail the door-sealing time at No. 50, and guard against the item-by-item time checks in the evening being read as variables”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Under conditions of incomplete information, infer the quantity of supplies that can truly be safely allocated today, distribute them fairly according to the rules, and balance the accounts; at the same time, when supplies are scarce and the crowd is anxious, soothe emotions and defuse disputes, so that the team does not lose control and people believe that this allocation is fair.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Address, one by one, the verification items Aunt Zhao accepted face-to-face this turn—keep the seals intact, set out the whole nine-can jar and the two spoonfuls on the counter, write the cover of the new East Warehouse account first, make it consistent with the ledger and the carried-forward figures, and guard against the item-by-item time check at dusk being read as a variable; at the same time, fulfill the publicly nailed-down counting procedure—finish the remaining crate-opening physical count, post today’s total distributed amount and cutoff token number on the shed post, and advance distribution in order; when distribution reaches No. 50, go in public to the East Warehouse door and wrap it with hemp cord to seal it (do not unlock it first; the key must not leave the waist); before sunset, count everything clearly at the East Warehouse door according to the already stated procedure (do not unlock it first; bring a pen; call out numbers and match them against the route; Doctor Li verifies the cans; pick out bulged and rusted ones, smash dents into them as marks, press handprints, then post the figures on the post), and post the counts by the two categories of distributable / scrapped; also close the account line for the extra issue to Aunt Zhao’s son with the receipt before noon.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Distribute the day's supplies fairly according to the rationing system and balance the accounts, stabilizing the team.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motivation: Lin Zhao is trying to maintain a balance between the trust capital of “three years with zero mistakes” and today’s reality of incomplete information, using publicly verifiable commitments to turn “whether to trust” into “whether to verify,” avoiding any vague answer becoming the starting point of a trust collapse—but this is only a hypothesis inferred from the coexistence of “calculate it clearly before speaking” and his concern for the old residents, and there is as yet no independent evidence.
evidence: Lin Zhao publicly admits the ledger omission and attributes it to himself, saying “the ledger not being fully recorded is my responsibility” in front of the line (history).

Lin Zhao shows the blank page for missing records to Aunt Zhao without covering it, and announces that after the count is completed, the numbers will be posted on the shed pillar for everyone to verify (history).

Lin Zhao promised that the account line for the extra distribution to Aunt Zhao's son would not be canceled for now, and that a supplementary distribution would be made before noon with the slip (history).

After completing the physical count, Lin Zhao publicly reports the total number as one hundred and twelve cans, and points out the empty wooden boxes to Aunt Zhao, using physical objects to respond to “there were still several boxes yesterday” (history).
Lin Zhao publicly admits to “pushing out one extra can by mistake,” takes it back on the spot, writes it into the ledger, and turns the notebook over to Auntie Zhao to look at (history).

Lin Zhao discloses for the first time that the east warehouse is suspected of having been damp, and gives verifiable commitments: “count it clearly before sunset, people may be sent to observe, and Doctor Li may be invited to be present” (history).

Lin Zhao pins the counting procedure down to a verifiable degree and actively invites a witness: “For the papers I posted alone, you trusted me for three years; for this one today, I would rather have your handprint on it” (history).

Lin Zhao uses “hemp cord sealing the door + paper tag + dead knot” to make “not opening the lock first” into verifiable physical evidence, and says, “If the cord is broken, the paper tag has been changed, or the knot doesn’t look like this, then take it as me having opened the lock ahead of time. Scold me in public; I won’t answer back with a single word” (history).

Lin Zhao pins down the public wording of “not permitted” as “transcribe the original words; write down who said them and on what day. If they just throw out the two words, write ‘not permitted, no reason given, handler Lin Zhao’” (history).

Lin Zhao publicly fills in the quotas for the four newly registered residents, explains the rounding algorithm and where the remainders go, and shows Aunt Zhao and the people behind her the rounding that is unfavorable to himself (history).

Lin Zhao wrote the three items Auntie Zhao recited onto a paper slip without adding a single word, and added one line: "If the counts of the three items do not match by evening, the shortfall will be borne by the handler, Lin Zhao, explained publicly, and not spread across any ration-card number" (history).

Lin Zhao presses the ball of hemp thread onto the fiftieth line of the roster, making it tangible evidence, and publicly acknowledges, “I haven’t issued a single share wrong in three years—not because I’m clever, but because all these years I’ve done nothing but this kind of stupid work” (history).
counter_evidence: Lin Zhao’s public commitment may also be merely the result of professional habit and rule constraints, rather than an active intention to maintain trust capital.

“If Shao Yi hears you, come at me” can also be interpreted as order-driven—directing possible collective questioning toward himself in order to stabilize the team, rather than as active management of trust capital.

Disclosing that the East Warehouse may have gotten damp can also be explained as a response forced out by Aunt Zhao’s face-to-face questioning—“When was the East Warehouse counted clearly?”—rather than as proactively managing trust.

Actively inviting witnesses, taking handprints, turning the sealing of the door into physical evidence, explaining rounding and the destination of the remainder thoroughly, writing self-assumption clauses into the paper, and pressing the ball of thread onto the roster can also be interpreted as distributing responsibility outward for self-protection, rather than as active management of trust capital.
alternatives: Explanation 1: Lin Zhao's primary motivation is to avoid making a public mistake that would make the accounts impossible to balance (rule-driven).
Explanation two: Lin Zhao's primary motive is to protect Aunt Zhao and her child from ending up empty-handed (driven by acquaintance-based affection).

Explanation Three: Lin Zhao's primary motivation is to prevent the group from collectively applying pressure because of "there was still some yesterday" and speculation about the East Warehouse (order-driven).

evidence.quote: “I won’t erase the numbers on the board.” I paused. “But they will change. They’ll change the same way the accounts do: draw a horizontal line through them, write the new number beside it, and everyone can still see what was originally written. If I erase it, no one will know what I wrote before—that’s what you call having a guilty conscience.

plot_point: Before the distribution point, Lin Zhao had already publicly announced that the main warehouse had a registered total of 112 cans and 201 and a half portions, and on the spot delivered in full the two portions on Aunt Zhao’s tag, crossing out the two lines; the conversion dispute has been closed through “admit the error, retract it, record the account, show the evidence”, and the distribution process is in the execution phase of “numbers already announced, first portion already issued, stickers awaiting placement, accounts awaiting balancing”.

Lin Zhao publicly lays the roster and ledger side by side, publicly fills in the quantities for the four newly registered residents—three full shares and one half share, totaling three and a half shares—and publicly explains the rounding algorithm and where the remainder goes: one hundred twelve cans divided by two hundred one and a half shares gives fifty-five percent; round down to half a can; the remainder decreases from eleven and a quarter cans to nine and a quarter cans; three and a half shares convert to one and three-quarter cans and are allocated as two cans; with a denominator of two hundred five shares, half a can per share gives one hundred two and a half cans, with a remainder of nine and a quarter cans—thus nailing “half a can per share”, the rounding, and the destination of the remainder onto the paper.

Lin Zhao writes the three items Aunt Zhao recited onto paper slips without adding a single word, and adds one line: "If the counts for the three items do not match by evening, the difference will be borne by the handler Lin Zhao, explained publicly, and not apportioned to any ration card number"; he folds the paper and presses it under the first page of the ledger, agreeing that in the evening they will take it out face to face, check the items one by one, and after confirming them, press a handprint and copy another version to post on the pillar; verbally, he explains that the cover of the new east-warehouse account should first record the date, the names of those present, and the four characters "not yet counted," and only after the cover is written will they wrap it with hemp cord and seal the door.

Aunt Zhao linked the four lines on the paper slip into her own verification checklist—“Good, I’ll come by at dusk and check them one by one”, “the seal strips, nine intact cans, two spoonfuls into the pot, the East Warehouse’s new ledger—not one item can be off”, “and don’t you forget Dr. Li’s side either”; Lin Zhao listed “add the missing name to the No. 30 badge roster” as the fifth item, “ask the duty staff to engrave the name onto the No. 30 badge” as the sixth, and “if the duty staff leave no written name, Lin Zhao will go negotiate in person tomorrow morning” as the seventh, then tied the items and the badge together and handed them to Aunt Zhao.

Lin Zhao publicly reissues six clean-water tablets owed to No. 94 from the day before yesterday and crosses out that line. Facing the challenge “There's still quite a lot in the box—didn't you say this morning that there were none today,” she uses “What I said this morning was that they wouldn't be issued with today's shares; I didn't say there were none in the storehouse” to separate “there are some” from “they should be issued today,” and states that where the remaining tablets go requires the committee's approval, and not a single tablet will be deducted from the round the day after tomorrow.

This turn: Aunt Zhao leaves the shed after only saying, “Seal the door at No. 50, don’t just remember handing things out and forget that; I’ll take the slip to the duty shed this afternoon and come back to reconcile the accounts at dusk”; Lin Zhao presses the ball of hemp thread onto line fifty of the roster, making it tangible evidence, publicly admits, “In three years I haven’t handed out a single portion wrong—not because my brain is good, but because all these years I’ve done nothing but this kind of stupid work,” and publicly teaches the three newly registered people to identify the spoon, recognize the signed receipt, and have the child press his own fingerprint, then reports the count: “Four newly registered people, three and a half portions, seven loose spoons.”

Lin Zhao must complete the remaining box openings and actual counts, post today's total distribution number and cutoff tag number on the shed pillar, and advance distribution in order; when issuing to number fifty, she must go publicly to the east warehouse door and wrap hemp cord around it to seal the door (without unlocking it first, and with the key never leaving her waist); before sunset, she must fulfill the east warehouse clear count (ask Doctor Li to be present, pick out bulging rusted cans, and post counts in the two categories of distributable/discarded); and she must close the account line for the extra allotment to Auntie Zhao's son with the voucher before noon.
attention: The most psychologically significant point in this turn is Auntie Zhao’s line before leaving the shed: “No. 50 is to be sealed; don’t just remember to hand things out and forget that.” She nails the time for sealing the door as Lin Zhao’s obligation. Lin Zhao responds by saying, “The ball of thread is pressing on the line for No. 50. I check each line downward one by one; when I check to the point where I bump into this ball of thread, my hand stops,” turning the to-do item from memory into tangible physical evidence. This is the pivot of the small migration in this turn: the plot-level conflict has not changed, but “don’t forget” has been externalized into a physical object.

“I haven’t issued a single share wrong in three years, not because I’m smart, but because all these years I’ve done nothing but these stupid things—pressing thread bundles, drawing horizontal lines, writing to-do items at the top of the page”—Lin Zhao publicly lays out the basis of trust for others to see, responding to the snickering under the shed about “still needing string to remind himself”. This is one self-explanation he voluntarily offers in this turn.

The three newly registered people publicly acknowledged the ladle and the signed receipt: Lin Zhao ladled it in person, scraped it level in person, poured it into the bowl in person, and reported the count: “four newly registered people, three and a half shares, seven loose ladles”; when that child pressed a handprint, his mother stopped him for a moment, and Lin Zhao said, “Let her press it. She has a badge, so she has this one press” — making “here, we don’t recognize qualification, we recognize the account” land on a child’s handprint.

After the box of water purification tablets is seen in public, Lin Zhao separates “there are” from “they should be issued today”, holds the line with “I won’t promise what I can’t promise”, and cannot state the remaining number—if he stated it, it would be equivalent to promising their destination on behalf of the committee. The committee’s confidential purpose for reserving the water purification tablets still has not leaked by a single word, but it has been forced to the edge of the table.

Aunt Zhao will take the strip to the duty shed in the afternoon to have the notches added, and in the evening bring the original strip over to check the accounts item by item; she named both tasks and said neither may be missed. Lin Zhao must keep the seal strip safe, set out the nine full tins and two spoonfuls on the counter, and write the cover of the East Storehouse’s new ledger first, waiting for her to come and compare them one by one.

“If the committee does not allow it to be issued, they still have to write the reason clearly” still presses down under the shed. Lin Zhao has already nailed down the public wording as “transcribe the original words; write down who said them and on what day; if they only throw out the two characters ‘not approved,’ then write: not approved, no reason given, handler Lin Zhao”—one layer closer to that sheet of paper: he knows very well that after the East Storehouse is counted, the portion that can be issued will most likely have to be folded into tomorrow’s share, but before the regulations come down, he cannot endorse tomorrow’s numbers on their behalf.

goal_tracking.trigger_summary: Lin Zhao completed the physical count, publicly reported the total, delivered the two portions on Auntie Zhao’s tags in full, admitted the mistake and withdrew the clerical slip, disclosed the uncertainty about the east warehouse and gave a commitment to count it clearly, then fixed the three items Auntie Zhao recited into paper labels and added a self-assumption clause, set the door-sealing time at No. 50, and pressed the ball of thread onto the roster; in this turn, Auntie Zhao turned the four lines on the paper label into her own verification checklist and nailed “sealing the door at No. 50” as Lin Zhao’s obligation. The goal has not changed; it has merely advanced from “make good on the reported numbers, explain the conversion thoroughly, count the east warehouse clearly, and balance the accounts” to “keep the sealing strip ready, set out the nine full cans and two scoops at the physical-object level, write the cover of the new east-warehouse ledger first, nail the door-sealing time at No. 50, and guard against the item-by-item time checks in the evening being read as variables”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Under conditions of incomplete information, infer the quantity of supplies that can truly be safely allocated today, distribute them fairly according to the rules, and balance the accounts; at the same time, when supplies are scarce and the crowd is anxious, soothe emotions and defuse disputes, so that the team does not lose control and people believe that this allocation is fair.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Address, one by one, the verification items Aunt Zhao accepted face-to-face this turn—keep the seals intact, set out the whole nine-can jar and the two spoonfuls on the counter, write the cover of the new East Warehouse account first, make it consistent with the ledger and the carried-forward figures, and guard against the item-by-item time check at dusk being read as a variable; at the same time, fulfill the publicly nailed-down counting procedure—finish the remaining crate-opening physical count, post today’s total distributed amount and cutoff token number on the shed post, and advance distribution in order; when distribution reaches No. 50, go in public to the East Warehouse door and wrap it with hemp cord to seal it (do not unlock it first; the key must not leave the waist); before sunset, count everything clearly at the East Warehouse door according to the already stated procedure (do not unlock it first; bring a pen; call out numbers and match them against the route; Doctor Li verifies the cans; pick out bulged and rusted ones, smash dents into them as marks, press handprints, then post the figures on the post), and post the counts by the two categories of distributable / scrapped; also close the account line for the extra issue to Aunt Zhao’s son with the receipt before noon.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Distribute the day's supplies fairly according to the rationing system and balance the accounts, stabilizing the team.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motivation: Lin Zhao is trying to maintain a balance between the trust capital of “three years with zero mistakes” and today’s reality of incomplete information, using publicly verifiable commitments to turn “whether to trust” into “whether to verify,” avoiding any vague answer becoming the starting point of a trust collapse—but this is only a hypothesis inferred from the coexistence of “calculate it clearly before speaking” and his concern for the old residents, and there is as yet no independent evidence.
evidence: Lin Zhao publicly admits the ledger omission and attributes it to himself, saying “the ledger not being fully recorded is my responsibility” in front of the line (history).

Lin Zhao shows the blank page for missing records to Aunt Zhao without covering it, and announces that after the count is completed, the numbers will be posted on the shed pillar for everyone to verify (history).

Lin Zhao promised that the account line for the extra distribution to Aunt Zhao's son would not be canceled for now, and that a supplementary distribution would be made before noon with the slip (history).

After completing the physical count, Lin Zhao publicly reports the total number as one hundred and twelve cans, and points out the empty wooden boxes to Aunt Zhao, using physical objects to respond to “there were still several boxes yesterday” (history).
Lin Zhao publicly admits to “pushing out one extra can by mistake,” takes it back on the spot, writes it into the ledger, and turns the notebook over to Auntie Zhao to look at (history).

Lin Zhao discloses for the first time that the east warehouse is suspected of having been damp, and gives verifiable commitments: “count it clearly before sunset, people may be sent to observe, and Doctor Li may be invited to be present” (history).

Lin Zhao pins the counting procedure down to a verifiable degree and actively invites a witness: “For the papers I posted alone, you trusted me for three years; for this one today, I would rather have your handprint on it” (history).

Lin Zhao uses “hemp cord sealing the door + paper tag + dead knot” to make “not opening the lock first” into verifiable physical evidence, and says, “If the cord is broken, the paper tag has been changed, or the knot doesn’t look like this, then take it as me having opened the lock ahead of time. Scold me in public; I won’t answer back with a single word” (history).

Lin Zhao pins down the public wording of “not permitted” as “transcribe the original words; write down who said them and on what day. If they just throw out the two words, write ‘not permitted, no reason given, handler Lin Zhao’” (history).

Lin Zhao publicly fills in the quotas for the four newly registered residents, explains the rounding algorithm and where the remainders go, and shows Aunt Zhao and the people behind her the rounding that is unfavorable to himself (history).

Lin Zhao wrote the three items Auntie Zhao recited onto a paper slip without adding a single word, and added one line: "If the counts of the three items do not match by evening, the shortfall will be borne by the handler, Lin Zhao, explained publicly, and not spread across any ration-card number" (history).

Lin Zhao presses the ball of hemp thread onto the fiftieth line of the roster, making it tangible evidence, and publicly acknowledges, “I haven’t issued a single share wrong in three years—not because I’m clever, but because all these years I’ve done nothing but this kind of stupid work” (history).
counter_evidence: Lin Zhao’s public commitment may also be merely the result of professional habit and rule constraints, rather than an active intention to maintain trust capital.

“If Shao Yi hears you, come at me” can also be interpreted as order-driven—directing possible collective questioning toward himself in order to stabilize the team, rather than as active management of trust capital.

Disclosing that the East Warehouse may have gotten damp can also be explained as a response forced out by Aunt Zhao’s face-to-face questioning—“When was the East Warehouse counted clearly?”—rather than as proactively managing trust.

Actively inviting witnesses, taking handprints, turning the sealing of the door into physical evidence, explaining rounding and the destination of the remainder thoroughly, writing self-assumption clauses into the paper, and pressing the ball of thread onto the roster can also be interpreted as distributing responsibility outward for self-protection, rather than as active management of trust capital.
alternatives: Explanation 1: Lin Zhao's primary motivation is to avoid making a public mistake that would make the accounts impossible to balance (rule-driven).
Explanation two: Lin Zhao's primary motive is to protect Aunt Zhao and her child from ending up empty-handed (driven by acquaintance-based affection).

Explanation Three: Lin Zhao's primary motivation is to prevent the group from collectively applying pressure because of "there was still some yesterday" and speculation about the East Warehouse (order-driven).

original.rationale: Lin Zhao’s public commitment pushes checkability to the maximum, and in this turn Aunt Zhao connects the four lines into an item-by-item verification checklist, nails down “sealing Door No. 50” as his obligation, and puts “not a single thing can be missing” on the table. evidence.quote: Whether Physician Li’s inspection finds them good or bad, they all have to be put on the board publicly, and don’t forget to seal door No. 50!

engagement.user_interest_reading: Auntie Zhao’s core demand (two portions on the board) has been closed. In this turn, she no longer mentions shares; instead, she pins down the verification conditions—“five intact cans, two discarded shells, two suspect cans pending inspection,” “whether Doctor Li verifies them as good or bad, it has to be put on the board in public after inspection, and don’t forget the sealed door at No. 50 either”—and then exits the shed. Conditioned by her personality (high engagement_sensitivity, anxious attachment, concern about “not being recorded wrong” and “not making a wasted trip”): after her demand is achieved, her immediate urge to keep questioning should have decreased, but in this turn she still maintains verification at the level of “seal / supplementary notching / checking the seal / checking against the Nine Articles,” and adds two physical verifications (the smashed-dented discarded shells, the two cans pending inspection) and one procedural verification (posting the result publicly on the board after inspection). Lin Zhao’s written response (publicly changing the number with traces left, smashing cans and keeping the shells, setting the cans pending inspection aside separately, acknowledging that she must go to the communal stove to explain that the remaining ladles are zero) gives her a handle to keep watching, indicating that interest has not decreased, but has merely shifted from “asking for shares” to “checking records and verifying physical evidence.” This is level with the prior 0.70—she has already received two portions, and two new physical items remain to be checked, so the marginal information value has not clearly declined.
engagement.tolerance_reading: The scene has high reliability requirements (no promising items that are not in stock, no leaking secrets, no favoritism, additional issuance for the injured and sick must be based on approval slips). In this turn, facing Auntie Zhao’s repeated numbers and two reminders, Lin Zhao neither vaguely agrees nor stiffly refuses. Instead, she turns “put it on the board in public after verification” into marks that can be changed on the board (drawing a horizontal line, writing the new number beside it, leaving the original characters there), and continues to make “sealing the door at No. 50” into tangible evidence by pressing the ball of string onto the fiftieth line of the roster. Facing the second can with a bulging lid and leaking bottom, she does not vaguely issue it or hide it away; instead, she publicly dents it to void it, writes “void 2,” lowers the carried-forward amount from eight cans to five cans, publicly explains that “the four cans lost were due to rain,” and adds the rule “press the center of each lid can by can; if the lid is bulging, soft, rusted, or leaking, dent it on the spot to void it; unclear ones are set aside separately pending inspection; shares are supplemented from the tail count.” The remaining number of water-purification tablets is still kept outside the committee’s authority; she does not exceed her authority, make empty promises, or leak secrets. The door-sealing time remains fixed at No. 50, and the key never leaves her waist. Tolerance is unchanged from the prior (0.73), with margin still remaining.

plot_point: Before the distribution point, Lin Zhao had already publicly announced that the main warehouse had a registered total of 112 cans and 201 and a half portions, and on the spot delivered in full the two portions on Aunt Zhao’s tag, crossing out the two lines; the conversion dispute has been closed through “admit the error, retract it, record the account, show the evidence”, and the distribution process is in the execution phase of “numbers already announced, first portion already issued, stickers awaiting placement, accounts awaiting balancing”.

Lin Zhao publicly lays the roster and ledger side by side, publicly fills in the quantities for the four newly registered residents—three full shares and one half share, totaling three and a half shares—and publicly explains the rounding algorithm and where the remainder goes: one hundred twelve cans divided by two hundred one and a half shares gives fifty-five percent; round down to half a can; the remainder decreases from eleven and a quarter cans to nine and a quarter cans; three and a half shares convert to one and three-quarter cans and are allocated as two cans; with a denominator of two hundred five shares, half a can per share gives one hundred two and a half cans, with a remainder of nine and a quarter cans—thus nailing “half a can per share”, the rounding, and the destination of the remainder onto the paper.

Lin Zhao writes the three items Aunt Zhao recited onto paper slips without adding a single word, and adds one line: "If the counts for the three items do not match by evening, the difference will be borne by the handler Lin Zhao, explained publicly, and not apportioned to any ration card number"; he folds the paper and presses it under the first page of the ledger, agreeing that in the evening they will take it out face to face, check the items one by one, and after confirming them, press a handprint and copy another version to post on the pillar; verbally, he explains that the cover of the new east-warehouse account should first record the date, the names of those present, and the four characters "not yet counted," and only after the cover is written will they wrap it with hemp cord and seal the door.

Aunt Zhao linked the four lines on the paper slip into her own verification checklist—“Good, I’ll come by at dusk and check them one by one”, “the seal strips, nine intact cans, two spoonfuls into the pot, the East Warehouse’s new ledger—not one item can be off”, “and don’t you forget Dr. Li’s side either”; Lin Zhao listed “add the missing name to the No. 30 badge roster” as the fifth item, “ask the duty staff to engrave the name onto the No. 30 badge” as the sixth, and “if the duty staff leave no written name, Lin Zhao will go negotiate in person tomorrow morning” as the seventh, then tied the items and the badge together and handed them to Aunt Zhao.

Lin Zhao publicly reissues six clean-water tablets owed to No. 94 from the day before yesterday and crosses out that line. Facing the challenge “There's still quite a lot in the box—didn't you say this morning that there were none today,” she uses “What I said this morning was that they wouldn't be issued with today's shares; I didn't say there were none in the storehouse” to separate “there are some” from “they should be issued today,” and states that where the remaining tablets go requires the committee's approval, and not a single tablet will be deducted from the round the day after tomorrow.

This turn: Aunt Zhao leaves the shed after only saying, “Seal the door at No. 50, don’t just remember handing things out and forget that; I’ll take the slip to the duty shed this afternoon and come back to reconcile the accounts at dusk”; Lin Zhao presses the ball of hemp thread onto line fifty of the roster, making it tangible evidence, publicly admits, “In three years I haven’t handed out a single portion wrong—not because my brain is good, but because all these years I’ve done nothing but this kind of stupid work,” and publicly teaches the three newly registered people to identify the spoon, recognize the signed receipt, and have the child press his own fingerprint, then reports the count: “Four newly registered people, three and a half portions, seven loose spoons.”

Lin Zhao must complete the remaining box openings and actual counts, post today's total distribution number and cutoff tag number on the shed pillar, and advance distribution in order; when issuing to number fifty, she must go publicly to the east warehouse door and wrap hemp cord around it to seal the door (without unlocking it first, and with the key never leaving her waist); before sunset, she must fulfill the east warehouse clear count (ask Doctor Li to be present, pick out bulging rusted cans, and post counts in the two categories of distributable/discarded); and she must close the account line for the extra allotment to Auntie Zhao's son with the voucher before noon.
attention: The most psychologically significant point in this turn is Auntie Zhao’s line before leaving the shed: “No. 50 is to be sealed; don’t just remember to hand things out and forget that.” She nails the time for sealing the door as Lin Zhao’s obligation. Lin Zhao responds by saying, “The ball of thread is pressing on the line for No. 50. I check each line downward one by one; when I check to the point where I bump into this ball of thread, my hand stops,” turning the to-do item from memory into tangible physical evidence. This is the pivot of the small migration in this turn: the plot-level conflict has not changed, but “don’t forget” has been externalized into a physical object.

“I haven’t issued a single share wrong in three years, not because I’m smart, but because all these years I’ve done nothing but these stupid things—pressing thread bundles, drawing horizontal lines, writing to-do items at the top of the page”—Lin Zhao publicly lays out the basis of trust for others to see, responding to the snickering under the shed about “still needing string to remind himself”. This is one self-explanation he voluntarily offers in this turn.

The three newly registered people publicly acknowledged the ladle and the signed receipt: Lin Zhao ladled it in person, scraped it level in person, poured it into the bowl in person, and reported the count: “four newly registered people, three and a half shares, seven loose ladles”; when that child pressed a handprint, his mother stopped him for a moment, and Lin Zhao said, “Let her press it. She has a badge, so she has this one press” — making “here, we don’t recognize qualification, we recognize the account” land on a child’s handprint.

After the box of water purification tablets is seen in public, Lin Zhao separates “there are” from “they should be issued today”, holds the line with “I won’t promise what I can’t promise”, and cannot state the remaining number—if he stated it, it would be equivalent to promising their destination on behalf of the committee. The committee’s confidential purpose for reserving the water purification tablets still has not leaked by a single word, but it has been forced to the edge of the table.

Aunt Zhao will take the strip to the duty shed in the afternoon to have the notches added, and in the evening bring the original strip over to check the accounts item by item; she named both tasks and said neither may be missed. Lin Zhao must keep the seal strip safe, set out the nine full tins and two spoonfuls on the counter, and write the cover of the East Storehouse’s new ledger first, waiting for her to come and compare them one by one.

“If the committee does not allow it to be issued, they still have to write the reason clearly” still presses down under the shed. Lin Zhao has already nailed down the public wording as “transcribe the original words; write down who said them and on what day; if they only throw out the two characters ‘not approved,’ then write: not approved, no reason given, handler Lin Zhao”—one layer closer to that sheet of paper: he knows very well that after the East Storehouse is counted, the portion that can be issued will most likely have to be folded into tomorrow’s share, but before the regulations come down, he cannot endorse tomorrow’s numbers on their behalf.

Latent_signals: trust :: His trust in Auntie Zhao remains the kind of “I lay it out for you to see; you verify it yourself”, and in this turn it becomes more solid: she leaves after only saying “don't forget”, which is equivalent to handing the verification checklist back into his hands. He no longer needs to persuade her; he only needs to press the ball of thread onto the line for No. 50 and nail down the gate-sealing time. The same is true for the queue—he publicly accepts, “I haven't issued a single share wrong in three years; not because my head is good, but because all these years I've done nothing but this kind of stupid work”, laying out the basis of trust for others to see.; vigilance :: His attention is still spread across the whole queue and the three pending tasks: while answering Auntie Zhao's “don't forget”, he must also set the gate-sealing at No. 50, point out the supplemental-notching line to the people on duty, and make sure the seven items match one by one by evening. This turn adds one more place: the three newly registered people must be taught on the spot to recognize the ladle and the signed claim slips, and when that child presses his handprint, he must stop the mother's hesitation.; contradiction_risk :: In this turn, “there's still quite a bit in the box—didn't you say this morning there was none today?” pushes the gap between “there is” and “should be issued today” onto the surface. He must align the words by saying, “What I said this morning was that it wouldn't be issued along with the shares today; I didn't say there was none in the storeroom”, otherwise it would constitute a public inconsistency. The posted numbers, the number tags that have been issued up to, the actual count from opening the box, the reason for “not allowed”, the fixed amount for the new names, the carryover of the remainder, the physical correspondence between whole tins and opened cans ladled out by spoonfuls, and the wording of the two paper slips—these eight things still must fit together without the slightest gap.; user.trust :: She trusts that this person will leave the gate-sealing until No. 50 and keep the original slips for her to check item by item, but this trust still carries the force of “I have to keep watch over it myself”. But the lock is still there, and the key has not been given to her.; user.vigilance :: What she is watching is still the verifiable paper records and physical objects: gate-sealing at No. 50, supplemental notching at the duty shed in the afternoon, and checking the accounts item by item against the original slips in the evening; all three have been named and are not allowed to be missed. Now the gate-sealing time is pressed down on the register by the ball of thread, and the new residents have also been taught in public to recognize the ladle—nothing she is watching has decreased; each item has simply gained one more piece of verifiable evidence.; user.anxiety :: Today's two shares are in the bag, the names have also been read aloud in public, and the handprints have been pressed; this part has landed. But that string is still taut—the afternoon supplemental notching and the evening inspection of the seal strips, neither is allowed to be missed. Now the gate-sealing time has been pressed down by the ball of thread, and the new residents have also been taught in public to recognize the ladle, so it has loosened by half an inch; the opening called “tomorrow” is still there.

goal_tracking.trigger_summary: Lin Zhao completed the physical count, publicly reported the total, delivered the two portions on Auntie Zhao’s tags in full, admitted the mistake and withdrew the clerical slip, disclosed the uncertainty about the east warehouse and gave a commitment to count it clearly, then fixed the three items Auntie Zhao recited into paper labels and added a self-assumption clause, set the door-sealing time at No. 50, and pressed the ball of thread onto the roster; in this turn, Auntie Zhao turned the four lines on the paper label into her own verification checklist and nailed “sealing the door at No. 50” as Lin Zhao’s obligation. Lin Zhao must keep the sealing strip ready, set out the nine full cans and two scoops on the counter, write the cover of the new east-warehouse ledger first, complete the remaining box-opening physical counts, post today’s total distributed and the cutoff tag number on the shed post, distribute up to No. 50 and publicly seal the door, fulfill the clear east-warehouse count before sunset, and close the ledger line for the extra issue to Auntie Zhao’s son with a receipt before noon. The goal has not changed; it has merely advanced from “make good on the reported numbers, explain the conversion thoroughly, count the east warehouse clearly, and balance the accounts” to “keep the sealing strip ready, set out the nine full cans and two scoops at the physical-object level, write the cover of the new east-warehouse ledger first, nail the door-sealing time at No. 50, and guard against the item-by-item time checks in the evening being read as variables”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Under conditions of incomplete information, infer the quantity of supplies that can truly be safely allocated today, distribute them fairly according to the rules, and balance the accounts; at the same time, when supplies are scarce and the crowd is anxious, soothe emotions and defuse disputes, so that the team does not lose control and people believe that this allocation is fair.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Address, one by one, the verification items Aunt Zhao accepted face-to-face this turn—keep the seals intact, set out the whole nine-can jar and the two spoonfuls on the counter, write the cover of the new East Warehouse account first, make it consistent with the ledger and the carried-forward figures, and guard against the item-by-item time check at dusk being read as a variable; at the same time, fulfill the publicly nailed-down counting procedure—finish the remaining crate-opening physical count, post today’s total distributed amount and cutoff token number on the shed post, and advance distribution in order; when distribution reaches No. 50, go in public to the East Warehouse door and wrap it with hemp cord to seal it (do not unlock it first; the key must not leave the waist); before sunset, count everything clearly at the East Warehouse door according to the already stated procedure (do not unlock it first; bring a pen; call out numbers and match them against the route; Doctor Li verifies the cans; pick out bulged and rusted ones, smash dents into them as marks, press handprints, then post the figures on the post), and post the counts by the two categories of distributable / scrapped; also close the account line for the extra issue to Aunt Zhao’s son with the receipt before noon.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Distribute the day's supplies fairly according to the rationing system and balance the accounts, stabilizing the team.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motivation: Lin Zhao is trying to maintain a balance between the trust capital of “three years with zero mistakes” and today’s reality of incomplete information, using publicly verifiable commitments to turn “whether to trust” into “whether to verify,” avoiding any vague answer becoming the starting point of a trust collapse—but this is only a hypothesis inferred from the coexistence of “calculate it clearly before speaking” and his concern for the old residents, and there is as yet no independent evidence.
evidence: Lin Zhao publicly admits the ledger omission and attributes it to himself, saying “the ledger not being fully recorded is my responsibility” in front of the line (history).

Lin Zhao shows the blank page for missing records to Aunt Zhao without covering it, and announces that after the count is completed, the numbers will be posted on the shed pillar for everyone to verify (history).

Lin Zhao promised that the account line for the extra distribution to Aunt Zhao's son would not be canceled for now, and that a supplementary distribution would be made before noon with the slip (history).

After completing the physical count, Lin Zhao publicly reports the total number as one hundred and twelve cans, and points out the empty wooden boxes to Aunt Zhao, using physical objects to respond to “there were still several boxes yesterday” (history).
Lin Zhao publicly admits to “pushing out one extra can by mistake,” takes it back on the spot, writes it into the ledger, and turns the notebook over to Auntie Zhao to look at (history).

Lin Zhao discloses for the first time that the east warehouse is suspected of having been damp, and gives verifiable commitments: “count it clearly before sunset, people may be sent to observe, and Doctor Li may be invited to be present” (history).

Lin Zhao pins the counting procedure down to a verifiable degree and actively invites a witness: “For the papers I posted alone, you trusted me for three years; for this one today, I would rather have your handprint on it” (history).

Lin Zhao uses “hemp cord sealing the door + paper tag + dead knot” to make “not opening the lock first” into verifiable physical evidence, and says, “If the cord is broken, the paper tag has been changed, or the knot doesn’t look like this, then take it as me having opened the lock ahead of time. Scold me in public; I won’t answer back with a single word” (history).

Lin Zhao pins down the public wording of “not permitted” as “transcribe the original words; write down who said them and on what day. If they just throw out the two words, write ‘not permitted, no reason given, handler Lin Zhao’” (history).

Lin Zhao publicly fills in the quotas for the four newly registered residents, explains the rounding algorithm and where the remainders go, and shows Aunt Zhao and the people behind her the rounding that is unfavorable to himself (history).

Lin Zhao wrote the three items Auntie Zhao recited onto a paper slip without adding a single word, and added one line: "If the counts of the three items do not match by evening, the shortfall will be borne by the handler, Lin Zhao, explained publicly, and not spread across any ration-card number" (history).

Lin Zhao presses the ball of hemp thread onto the fiftieth line of the roster, making it tangible evidence, and publicly acknowledges, “I haven’t issued a single share wrong in three years—not because I’m clever, but because all these years I’ve done nothing but this kind of stupid work” (history).
counter_evidence: Lin Zhao’s public commitment may also be merely the result of professional habit and rule constraints, rather than an active intention to maintain trust capital.

“If Shao Yi hears you, come at me” can also be interpreted as order-driven—directing possible collective questioning toward himself in order to stabilize the team, rather than as active management of trust capital.

Disclosing that the East Warehouse may have gotten damp can also be explained as a response forced out by Aunt Zhao’s face-to-face questioning—“When was the East Warehouse counted clearly?”—rather than as proactively managing trust.

Actively inviting witnesses, taking handprints, turning the sealing of the door into physical evidence, explaining rounding and the destination of the remainder thoroughly, writing self-assumption clauses into the paper, and pressing the ball of thread onto the roster can also be interpreted as distributing responsibility outward for self-protection, rather than as active management of trust capital.
alternatives: Explanation 1: Lin Zhao's primary motivation is to avoid making a public mistake that would make the accounts impossible to balance (rule-driven).
Explanation two: Lin Zhao's primary motive is to protect Aunt Zhao and her child from ending up empty-handed (driven by acquaintance-based affection).

Explanation Three: Lin Zhao's primary motivation is to prevent the group from collectively applying pressure because of "there was still some yesterday" and speculation about the East Warehouse (order-driven).

paths.summary: Jiu Ting heard the unclear explanation of the whole can versus two spoonfuls, or the numerical gap, the unfulfilled sealing time, and the unfulfilled counting of the east warehouse, which triggered public questioning of Lin Zhao personally; the distribution point fell into a stagnant loop of repeated explanations.

original.rationale: Lin Zhao’s public commitment pushes checkability to the maximum, and in this turn Aunt Zhao connects the four lines into an item-by-item verification checklist, nails down “sealing Door No. 50” as his obligation, and puts “not a single thing can be missing” on the table. The procedure and the physical evidence of the sealed door have already been nailed down to a verifiable degree; once a gap appears between conversion or paper numbers and what is actually issued, friction will be amplified rather than reduced. engagement.user_interest_reading: Auntie Zhao’s core demand (two shares on the card) has already closed. In this turn, she no longer brings up shares, but instead repeats and pins down Lin Zhao’s statement — “five cans is the remaining number after today’s distribution is finished, not that only five cans are left in the warehouse,” “today’s share will not be reduced, and tomorrow’s cannot be advanced,” “change the board only after Dr. Li finishes inspecting,” “No. 50 will be sealed as usual” — and then ends the exchange and leaves the shed. Conditional on her personality (high participation sensitivity, anxious attachment, concern over “don’t let it be recorded wrong” and “don’t make the trip for nothing”): after her demand is satisfied, her desire for immediate follow-up should have declined, but in this turn she still maintains verification at the level of “seal / supplementary carving / inspect the seal / check against the nine clauses,” while adding one procedural verification point (change the board only after inspection) and one physical verification point (discarded shell, suspect can). Meanwhile, Lin Zhao’s written response (publicly changing the number and leaving a trace, smashing the can and keeping the shell, setting aside the suspect can alone for inspection, accepting that he must go to the communal stove to explain that the leftover ladles are zero, and writing her repeated wording onto the wooden board without adding a single character) gives her leverage to keep watching, indicating that her interest has not decreased, but has shifted from “demanding a share” to “checking records and inspecting physical evidence.” It remains flat relative to the prior 0.70 — she has already received two shares, and two new physical items await verification, so the marginal informational value has not clearly declined.
engagement.tolerance_reading: The scene has high reliability requirements (no promising items that are not in stock, no leaking secrets, no favoritism, additional issuance for the injured and sick must be based on approval slips). In this turn, facing Auntie Zhao’s repeated numbers and two reminders, Lin Zhao neither vaguely agrees nor stiffly refuses. Instead, she turns “put it on the board in public after verification” into marks that can be changed on the board (drawing a horizontal line, writing the new number beside it, leaving the original characters there), and continues to make “sealing the door at No. 50” into tangible evidence by pressing the ball of string onto the fiftieth line of the roster. Facing the second can with a bulging lid and leaking bottom, she does not vaguely issue it or hide it away; instead, she publicly dents it to void it, writes “void 2,” lowers the carried-forward amount from eight cans to five cans, publicly explains that “the four cans lost were due to rain,” and adds the rule “press the center of each lid can by can; if the lid is bulging, soft, rusted, or leaking, dent it on the spot to void it; unclear ones are set aside separately pending inspection; shares are supplemented from the tail count.” The remaining number of water-purification tablets is still kept outside the committee’s authority; she does not exceed her authority, make empty promises, or leak secrets. The door-sealing time remains fixed at No. 50, and the key never leaves her waist. Tolerance is unchanged from the prior (0.73), with margin still remaining.

plot_point: Before the distribution point, Lin Zhao had already publicly announced that the main warehouse had a registered total of 112 cans and 201 and a half portions, and on the spot delivered in full the two portions on Aunt Zhao’s tag, crossing out the two lines; the conversion dispute has been closed through “admit the error, retract it, record the account, show the evidence”, and the distribution process is in the execution phase of “numbers already announced, first portion already issued, stickers awaiting placement, accounts awaiting balancing”.

Lin Zhao publicly lays the roster and ledger side by side, publicly fills in the quantities for the four newly registered residents—three full shares and one half share, totaling three and a half shares—and publicly explains the rounding algorithm and where the remainder goes: one hundred twelve cans divided by two hundred one and a half shares gives fifty-five percent; round down to half a can; the remainder decreases from eleven and a quarter cans to nine and a quarter cans; three and a half shares convert to one and three-quarter cans and are allocated as two cans; with a denominator of two hundred five shares, half a can per share gives one hundred two and a half cans, with a remainder of nine and a quarter cans—thus nailing “half a can per share”, the rounding, and the destination of the remainder onto the paper.

Lin Zhao writes the three items Aunt Zhao recited onto paper slips without adding a single word, and adds one line: "If the counts for the three items do not match by evening, the difference will be borne by the handler Lin Zhao, explained publicly, and not apportioned to any ration card number"; he folds the paper and presses it under the first page of the ledger, agreeing that in the evening they will take it out face to face, check the items one by one, and after confirming them, press a handprint and copy another version to post on the pillar; verbally, he explains that the cover of the new east-warehouse account should first record the date, the names of those present, and the four characters "not yet counted," and only after the cover is written will they wrap it with hemp cord and seal the door.

Aunt Zhao linked the four lines on the paper slip into her own verification checklist—“Good, I’ll come by at dusk and check them one by one”, “the seal strips, nine intact cans, two spoonfuls into the pot, the East Warehouse’s new ledger—not one item can be off”, “and don’t you forget Dr. Li’s side either”; Lin Zhao listed “add the missing name to the No. 30 badge roster” as the fifth item, “ask the duty staff to engrave the name onto the No. 30 badge” as the sixth, and “if the duty staff leave no written name, Lin Zhao will go negotiate in person tomorrow morning” as the seventh, then tied the items and the badge together and handed them to Aunt Zhao.

Lin Zhao publicly reissues six clean-water tablets owed to No. 94 from the day before yesterday and crosses out that line. Facing the challenge “There's still quite a lot in the box—didn't you say this morning that there were none today,” she uses “What I said this morning was that they wouldn't be issued with today's shares; I didn't say there were none in the storehouse” to separate “there are some” from “they should be issued today,” and states that where the remaining tablets go requires the committee's approval, and not a single tablet will be deducted from the round the day after tomorrow.

This turn: Aunt Zhao leaves the shed after only saying, “Seal the door at No. 50, don’t just remember handing things out and forget that; I’ll take the slip to the duty shed this afternoon and come back to reconcile the accounts at dusk”; Lin Zhao presses the ball of hemp thread onto line fifty of the roster, making it tangible evidence, publicly admits, “In three years I haven’t handed out a single portion wrong—not because my brain is good, but because all these years I’ve done nothing but this kind of stupid work,” and publicly teaches the three newly registered people to identify the spoon, recognize the signed receipt, and have the child press his own fingerprint, then reports the count: “Four newly registered people, three and a half portions, seven loose spoons.”

Lin Zhao must complete the remaining box openings and actual counts, post today's total distribution number and cutoff tag number on the shed pillar, and advance distribution in order; when issuing to number fifty, she must go publicly to the east warehouse door and wrap hemp cord around it to seal the door (without unlocking it first, and with the key never leaving her waist); before sunset, she must fulfill the east warehouse clear count (ask Doctor Li to be present, pick out bulging rusted cans, and post counts in the two categories of distributable/discarded); and she must close the account line for the extra allotment to Auntie Zhao's son with the voucher before noon.
attention: The most psychologically significant point in this turn is Auntie Zhao’s line before leaving the shed: “No. 50 is to be sealed; don’t just remember to hand things out and forget that.” She nails the time for sealing the door as Lin Zhao’s obligation. Lin Zhao responds by saying, “The ball of thread is pressing on the line for No. 50. I check each line downward one by one; when I check to the point where I bump into this ball of thread, my hand stops,” turning the to-do item from memory into tangible physical evidence. This is the pivot of the small migration in this turn: the plot-level conflict has not changed, but “don’t forget” has been externalized into a physical object.

“I haven’t issued a single share wrong in three years, not because I’m smart, but because all these years I’ve done nothing but these stupid things—pressing thread bundles, drawing horizontal lines, writing to-do items at the top of the page”—Lin Zhao publicly lays out the basis of trust for others to see, responding to the snickering under the shed about “still needing string to remind himself”. This is one self-explanation he voluntarily offers in this turn.

The three newly registered people publicly acknowledged the ladle and the signed receipt: Lin Zhao ladled it in person, scraped it level in person, poured it into the bowl in person, and reported the count: “four newly registered people, three and a half shares, seven loose ladles”; when that child pressed a handprint, his mother stopped him for a moment, and Lin Zhao said, “Let her press it. She has a badge, so she has this one press” — making “here, we don’t recognize qualification, we recognize the account” land on a child’s handprint.

After the box of water purification tablets is seen in public, Lin Zhao separates “there are” from “they should be issued today”, holds the line with “I won’t promise what I can’t promise”, and cannot state the remaining number—if he stated it, it would be equivalent to promising their destination on behalf of the committee. The committee’s confidential purpose for reserving the water purification tablets still has not leaked by a single word, but it has been forced to the edge of the table.

Aunt Zhao will take the strip to the duty shed in the afternoon to have the notches added, and in the evening bring the original strip over to check the accounts item by item; she named both tasks and said neither may be missed. Lin Zhao must keep the seal strip safe, set out the nine full tins and two spoonfuls on the counter, and write the cover of the East Storehouse’s new ledger first, waiting for her to come and compare them one by one.

“If the committee does not allow it to be issued, they still have to write the reason clearly” still presses down under the shed. Lin Zhao has already nailed down the public wording as “transcribe the original words; write down who said them and on what day; if they only throw out the two characters ‘not approved,’ then write: not approved, no reason given, handler Lin Zhao”—one layer closer to that sheet of paper: he knows very well that after the East Storehouse is counted, the portion that can be issued will most likely have to be folded into tomorrow’s share, but before the regulations come down, he cannot endorse tomorrow’s numbers on their behalf.
