Lin Zhao must keep the sealing strip ready, set out the nine full cans and two scoops on the counter, write the cover of the new east-warehouse ledger first, complete the remaining box-opening physical counts, post today’s total distributed and the cutoff tag number on the shed post, distribute up to No. 50 and publicly seal the door, fulfill the clear east-warehouse count before sunset, and close the ledger line for the extra issue to Auntie Zhao’s son with a receipt before noon. The goal has not changed; it has merely advanced from “make good on the reported numbers, explain the conversion thoroughly, count the east warehouse clearly, and balance the accounts” to “keep the sealing strip ready, set out the nine full cans and two scoops at the physical-object level, write the cover of the new east-warehouse ledger first, nail the door-sealing time at No. 50, and guard against the item-by-item time checks in the evening being read as variables”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Under conditions of incomplete information, infer the quantity of supplies that can truly be safely allocated today, distribute them fairly according to the rules, and balance the accounts; at the same time, when supplies are scarce and the crowd is anxious, soothe emotions and defuse disputes, so that the team does not lose control and people believe that this allocation is fair.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Address, one by one, the verification items Aunt Zhao accepted face-to-face this turn—keep the seals intact, set out the whole nine-can jar and the two spoonfuls on the counter, write the cover of the new East Warehouse account first, make it consistent with the ledger and the carried-forward figures, and guard against the item-by-item time check at dusk being read as a variable; at the same time, fulfill the publicly nailed-down counting procedure—finish the remaining crate-opening physical count, post today’s total distributed amount and cutoff token number on the shed post, and advance distribution in order; when distribution reaches No. 50, go in public to the East Warehouse door and wrap it with hemp cord to seal it (do not unlock it first; the key must not leave the waist); before sunset, count everything clearly at the East Warehouse door according to the already stated procedure (do not unlock it first; bring a pen; call out numbers and match them against the route; Doctor Li verifies the cans; pick out bulged and rusted ones, smash dents into them as marks, press handprints, then post the figures on the post), and post the counts by the two categories of distributable / scrapped; also close the account line for the extra issue to Aunt Zhao’s son with the receipt before noon.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Distribute the day's supplies fairly according to the rationing system and balance the accounts, stabilizing the team.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motivation: Lin Zhao is trying to maintain a balance between the trust capital of “three years with zero mistakes” and today’s reality of incomplete information, using publicly verifiable commitments to turn “whether to trust” into “whether to verify,” avoiding any vague answer becoming the starting point of a trust collapse—but this is only a hypothesis inferred from the coexistence of “calculate it clearly before speaking” and his concern for the old residents, and there is as yet no independent evidence.
evidence: Lin Zhao publicly admits the ledger omission and attributes it to himself, saying “the ledger not being fully recorded is my responsibility” in front of the line (history).

Lin Zhao shows the blank page for missing records to Aunt Zhao without covering it, and announces that after the count is completed, the numbers will be posted on the shed pillar for everyone to verify (history).

Lin Zhao promised that the account line for the extra distribution to Aunt Zhao's son would not be canceled for now, and that a supplementary distribution would be made before noon with the slip (history).

After completing the physical count, Lin Zhao publicly reports the total number as one hundred and twelve cans, and points out the empty wooden boxes to Aunt Zhao, using physical objects to respond to “there were still several boxes yesterday” (history).
Lin Zhao publicly admits to “pushing out one extra can by mistake,” takes it back on the spot, writes it into the ledger, and turns the notebook over to Auntie Zhao to look at (history).

Lin Zhao discloses for the first time that the east warehouse is suspected of having been damp, and gives verifiable commitments: “count it clearly before sunset, people may be sent to observe, and Doctor Li may be invited to be present” (history).

Lin Zhao pins the counting procedure down to a verifiable degree and actively invites a witness: “For the papers I posted alone, you trusted me for three years; for this one today, I would rather have your handprint on it” (history).

Lin Zhao uses “hemp cord sealing the door + paper tag + dead knot” to make “not opening the lock first” into verifiable physical evidence, and says, “If the cord is broken, the paper tag has been changed, or the knot doesn’t look like this, then take it as me having opened the lock ahead of time. Scold me in public; I won’t answer back with a single word” (history).

Lin Zhao pins down the public wording of “not permitted” as “transcribe the original words; write down who said them and on what day. If they just throw out the two words, write ‘not permitted, no reason given, handler Lin Zhao’” (history).

Lin Zhao publicly fills in the quotas for the four newly registered residents, explains the rounding algorithm and where the remainders go, and shows Aunt Zhao and the people behind her the rounding that is unfavorable to himself (history).

Lin Zhao wrote the three items Auntie Zhao recited onto a paper slip without adding a single word, and added one line: "If the counts of the three items do not match by evening, the shortfall will be borne by the handler, Lin Zhao, explained publicly, and not spread across any ration-card number" (history).

Lin Zhao presses the ball of hemp thread onto the fiftieth line of the roster, making it tangible evidence, and publicly acknowledges, “I haven’t issued a single share wrong in three years—not because I’m clever, but because all these years I’ve done nothing but this kind of stupid work” (history).
counter_evidence: Lin Zhao’s public commitment may also be merely the result of professional habit and rule constraints, rather than an active intention to maintain trust capital.

“If Shao Yi hears you, come at me” can also be interpreted as order-driven—directing possible collective questioning toward himself in order to stabilize the team, rather than as active management of trust capital.

Disclosing that the East Warehouse may have gotten damp can also be explained as a response forced out by Aunt Zhao’s face-to-face questioning—“When was the East Warehouse counted clearly?”—rather than as proactively managing trust.

Actively inviting witnesses, taking handprints, turning the sealing of the door into physical evidence, explaining rounding and the destination of the remainder thoroughly, writing self-assumption clauses into the paper, and pressing the ball of thread onto the roster can also be interpreted as distributing responsibility outward for self-protection, rather than as active management of trust capital.
alternatives: Explanation 1: Lin Zhao's primary motivation is to avoid making a public mistake that would make the accounts impossible to balance (rule-driven).
Explanation two: Lin Zhao's primary motive is to protect Aunt Zhao and her child from ending up empty-handed (driven by acquaintance-based affection).

Explanation Three: Lin Zhao's primary motivation is to prevent the group from collectively applying pressure because of "there was still some yesterday" and speculation about the East Warehouse (order-driven).

"On the way won't do."

"Number twenty-nine collecting on behalf of number thirty—I approved it, because of two things: first, number thirty, Zhao Chengan, is sick in bed. Doctor Li has it recorded. The two lines are consecutive on the roster: two mouths behind one door."
"Old Zhou's family is another household, another door. You and his family—your token numbers aren't consecutive, and the roster entries aren't consecutive.
"**Number thirty-eight, Zhou family: today's share retained, to be collected by the person herself or by a same-household token holder. Valid for the day; void after warehouse close at sunset.**"
"One spoon. Forty-seven, record: number thirty-six, one share, loose spoon two. Number thirty-eight's share retained today, not issued, not ticked."

evidence: Lin Zhao publicly admits the ledger omission and attributes it to himself, saying “the ledger not being fully recorded is my responsibility” in front of the line (history).

Lin Zhao shows the blank page for missing records to Aunt Zhao without covering it, and announces that after the count is completed, the numbers will be posted on the shed pillar for everyone to verify (history).

counter_evidence: Lin Zhao’s public commitment may also be merely the result of professional habit and rule constraints, rather than an active intention to maintain trust capital.

Actively inviting witnesses, taking handprints, turning the sealing of the door into physical evidence, explaining rounding and the destination of the remainder thoroughly, writing self-assumption clauses into the paper, and pressing the ball of thread onto the roster can also be interpreted as distributing responsibility outward for self-protection, rather than as active management of trust capital.
